configurations.name: riskerm
configurations.//: autoPort lets a second session run alongside the first rather than failing on a port the other holds. Nothing here needs a fixed port — no OAuth callback, webhook or CORS origin is pinned to localhost:8123. The sh wrapper is load-bearing: `php artisan serve` reads SERVER_PORT, not PORT (ServeCommand.php), so simply dropping the flag would leave Laravel on its default 8000 while the harness proxied to the assigned port and found nothing — a server that starts, looks healthy and serves no one.
runtimeArgs: export PATH="/Users/mac/Library/Application Support/Herd/bin:$PATH" && php artisan serve --host=127.0.0.1 --port=${PORT:-8123}

configurations.name: riskerm-e2e-mysql8
configurations.//: Serves against the Docker MySQL 8 container riskerm-mysql8 (127.0.0.1:3307, root/root), database risk_e2e_erm, for when XAMPP MariaDB is down. php -S rather than artisan serve because artisan serve passes only an allowlist of env vars to its child, so DB_* overrides would be dropped and .env's 3306 used.
runtimeArgs: export PATH="/Users/mac/Library/Application Support/Herd/bin:$PATH" DB_PORT=3307 DB_PASSWORD=root DB_DATABASE=risk_e2e_erm QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-8124} && cd public && php -S 127.0.0.1:${PORT:-8124} ../vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/resources/server.php
